data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_Free
data.value: Two or more participants, in any role. In round 1 each one makes a proposal. Then they argue with objections and replies. The independent reviewer (judge) picks one proposal or says "unresolved".

data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_Adversarial
data.value: At least one proponent and one critic are needed. The critic looks for errors, contradictions, risks and broken requirements. The proponent replies.

data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_ArchitectureReview
data.value: Two or more participants, each with a design of their own. They are compared on maintainability, security, performance, cost and complexity, and on your criteria.

data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_ImplementationAudit
data.value: One proponent defends the delivery and at least one critic is needed. A finished run is debated. Its saved version (commit) and its requirements are reviewed.

data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_OrchestratorReview
data.value: Two or more reviewers, critics or panelists. They review the history of a run and the auditor's report, with the fixed requirements orq-1 to orq-7.

data.name: Debate_ModeHelp_Tribunal
data.value: Two or more panelists, and only panelists. Each one evaluates on their own, with no discussion. The judge sums up all the evaluations.

data.name: Debate_Judgment_Converged
data.value: the positions agree: everyone marked their contribution as finished

data.name: Debate_Judgment_TurnMissing

data.name: Debate_Judgment_Tribunal

data.name: Debate_JudgingHelp_IndependentJudge
data.value: A judge from a company that neither produced the work nor takes part in the debate. It is the strict rule, with no exceptions.

data.name: Debate_JudgingHelp_CrossVendorPanel
data.value: One judge from each participant's company. It is an exception to the participants rule, not full independence. If both agree, their decision stands. If they disagree, you decide.

data.name: Debate_JudgingHelp_NonProducerJudge
data.value: A judge from the company that did not produce the work, even if it is a participant's company. It is an exception to the participants rule for that company.

data.name: Debate_Waiver

data.name: Info_Debates_What
data.value: Here several agents argue a question and an independent reviewer (judge) decides. Each debate spends your plan's usage limit. That is why you first see the settings and the estimate, and you approve it.

data.name: Info_Debates_Actions
data.value: Open a debate from the history to read it. Press "New debate" to prepare one. Resume an interrupted debate: it asks for your approval. Filter the history by mode.

data.name: Info_Verdict_What
data.value: It is the judge's answer: whether it approves, asks for changes or rejects, and why. Each requirement shows its status and the saved evidence it cites. If the judge breaks a rule, you will see it marked.

data.name: Info_Verdict_Actions
data.value: See which requirements are met and which are not. Open the saved evidence the judge cites. Press "Challenge" if you do not agree. Press "Create corrective tasks" to ask the orchestrator for the fixes. Decide yourself if the panel does not agree.

data.name: Info_Challenge_What
data.value: If you think a verdict is wrong, you can challenge it. A review debate with two sides is opened. Nothing is delivered by itself: if the result turns into an approval, you accept it.

data.name: Info_Challenge_Actions
data.value: Write why you challenge: it is saved as a note of yours. Choose who defends the verdict and who defends the challenge. Press "Prepare" to see who judges and the estimate. Press "Challenge" and approve to open the review.
